purpose: Teach: 挙式/原宿/マフィア/マドリード/ハローワーク/フェラーリ/軽井沢/種子

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんとの挙式は思い出深い
lines.en: You know, Gran, when I was young, my father's wedding day — I remember it so clearly.
lines.style: Soft, distant gaze into memory. Slow, measured pace. Gentle nostalgia in the voice, like holding something precious and fragile. Slight pause before speaking.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、原宿の竹下通りを歩かれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: That's right, and don't you remember walking down Takeshita Street in Harajuku back then, dear?
lines.style: Warm, gentle correction with a glimmer of knowing humor. Speaking to him as though reminding an old friend of something wonderful they share. Tender cadence on the final word.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがマフィア映画にお詳しかった
lines.en: Gran, I remember when my father really knew those mafia films inside and out.
lines.style: The same wistful distance, but with a thread of quiet amusement underneath. As if recalling something oddly specific about someone he loved. Voice doesn't rise — stays in that contemplative register.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、新婚旅行でマドリードに行ったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And our honeymoon in Madrid — you were the one who wanted to go there, weren't you, dear?
lines.style: Playful ownership in the correction. She's gently reminding him it was her idea. Warm and almost teasing, the way longtime partners speak. Slight lilt of affection on 'dear.'

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがハローワークに通われた
lines.en: Gran, I think of how my father used to go to the employment office those days.
lines.style: Still wistful, but the wistfulness has a different weight now — something quieter, perhaps more private. The pace doesn't rush. There's acceptance in the tone.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、フェラーリの雑誌をお買いになってたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: You were the one who bought those Ferrari magazines, weren't you? Don't pretend you weren't.
lines.style: Loving mockery. She's caught him out or is playfully teasing him about his own forgotten vanities. Voice has warmth and humor layered together. Light and knowing.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが軽井沢で休養された
lines.en: Gran, when we were younger, my father used to rest in Karuizawa.
lines.style: The wistfulness has deepened now into something quieter, almost meditative. Each phrase is given space. The voice settles lower, more intimate. Trails off gently.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お庭で野菜の種子をご自分で蒔かれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you're the one who planted those vegetable seeds in the garden with your own hands, weren't you, dear?
lines.style: Soft, close, intimate. As if speaking into the space between them after many years together. Tender without sentimentality. A small smile in the voice. Fades gently at the end.
